topic: House Rent Allowance (HRA) exemption for an employee who pays rent for a home that the employee does not own; available under the old tax regime subject to conditions
limit_amount: Least of: actual HRA received; rent paid minus 10% of salary; 50% of salary for Delhi, Mumbai, Kolkata or Chennai, otherwise 40% of salary

topic: Standard deduction from salary or pension income
limit_amount: Up to ₹50,000 under the old tax regime or ₹75,000 under the new tax regime, limited to the amount of salary where lower

topic: Deduction for employment tax or professional tax actually paid by the employee; available under the old tax regime and not deductible under the new tax regime
limit_amount: Actual professional tax paid during the year; no separate fixed rupee cap in this provision; not available under section 115BAC new regime

topic: Deduction for interest paid on borrowed capital for a house property
limit_amount: For a qualifying self-occupied property under the old regime, up to ₹2,00,000; specified cases are limited to ₹30,000. Let-out property and new-regime treatment have separate rules

topic: Deduction for eligible payments and investments such as life insurance premium, provident fund, tuition fees, National Savings Certificates and eligible housing-loan principal repayment; old regime only
limit_amount: Part of the combined ₹1,50,000 limit shared with sections 80CCC and 80CCD(1)

topic: Deduction for qualifying contribution to an annuity pension plan of LIC or another insurer; old regime only
limit_amount: Included in the combined ₹1,50,000 limit shared with sections 80C and 80CCD(1)

topic: Deduction for an individual's own eligible contribution to the National Pension System (NPS); old regime only
limit_amount: Employee: up to 10% of salary; self-employed: up to 20% of gross total income; also subject to the combined ₹1,50,000 limit with sections 80C and 80CCC

topic: Additional deduction for an individual's eligible own contribution to NPS, separate from the section 80CCD(1) deduction; old regime only
limit_amount: Additional deduction up to ₹50,000

topic: Deduction for an employer's eligible contribution to the employee's NPS account; available under both tax regimes subject to conditions
limit_amount: Up to 14% of salary under the new regime; under the old regime, generally 10% for non-government employers and 14% for Central or State Government employers

topic: Deduction for eligible health-insurance premiums and preventive health check-ups for self, spouse, dependent children and parents; old regime only
limit_amount: Generally up to ₹25,000 for self/family and ₹25,000 for parents; each limit can increase to ₹50,000 where the relevant insured person is a senior citizen. Preventive check-up up to ₹5,000 is included within the limit

topic: Flat deduction for eligible maintenance, medical treatment, training or rehabilitation of a dependent person with disability, subject to conditions; old regime only
limit_amount: ₹75,000; ₹1,25,000 for a dependent with severe disability

topic: Deduction for eligible expenditure on treatment of specified diseases for self or a qualifying dependent; old regime only
limit_amount: Up to ₹40,000; up to ₹1,00,000 for a senior citizen, subject to conditions and reductions for reimbursements

topic: Deduction for interest paid on an eligible education loan for higher studies of self or a qualifying relative; principal repayment is not deductible under this section; old regime only
limit_amount: Eligible interest actually paid, with no fixed rupee ceiling, for up to 8 consecutive assessment years beginning with the year interest repayment starts or until interest is fully paid, whichever is earlier

topic: Deduction for donations to specified funds and approved charitable institutions; deduction percentage and qualifying limits depend on the recipient; old regime only
limit_amount: Generally 50% or 100% of eligible donation, with or without qualifying limits depending on the approved fund or institution; cash donations above ₹2,000 are not eligible

topic: Deduction for rent paid by an individual who does not receive HRA, subject to residence and ownership conditions and filing Form 10BA; old regime only
limit_amount: Least of: rent paid minus 10% of adjusted total income; 25% of adjusted total income; or ₹5,000 per month

topic: Deduction for eligible interest earned on savings accounts by an individual or HUF other than a senior citizen; old regime only
limit_amount: Up to ₹10,000; applies to qualifying savings-account interest, not fixed/time-deposit interest

topic: Deduction for eligible interest on deposits earned by a resident senior citizen; old regime only
limit_amount: Up to ₹50,000 on qualifying interest from deposits with banks, co-operative banks or post offices

topic: Flat deduction for a resident individual taxpayer certified as a person with disability; this concerns the taxpayer's own disability, unlike section 80DD for a dependent; old regime only
limit_amount: ₹75,000; ₹1,25,000 for severe disability

topic: Tax rebate for an eligible resident individual; rebate limits differ between the old and new tax regimes for AY 2026-27
limit_amount: New regime: up to ₹60,000 if total income does not exceed ₹12,00,000; old regime: up to ₹12,500 if total income does not exceed ₹5,00,000; subject to statutory conditions

topic: Provision governing the concessional new tax regime, which is the default regime for eligible individuals; eligible taxpayers may opt for the old regime subject to applicable rules
